claim: Stress granules are non-membrane-bound RNA-protein granules that assemble through phase separation in response to cellular stress.
source: Stress granules (SGs) are non-membrane-bound RNA-protein granules that assemble through phase separation in response to cellular stress.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about stress granules that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Disturbances in stress granule dynamics have been implicated as a primary driver of neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD).
source: Disturbances in SG dynamics have been implicated as a primary driver of neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature in the field, as indicated in the Introduction section.

claim: OptoGranules is a light-inducible stress granule system based on optogenetic multimerization of G3BP1.
source: Here we introduce a light-inducible SG system, termed OptoGranules, based on optogenetic multimerization of G3BP1, which is an essential scaffold protein for SG assembly.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study describing the development of the OptoGranules system.

claim: G3BP1 is an essential scaffold protein for stress granule assembly.
source: Here we introduce a light-inducible SG system, termed OptoGranules, based on optogenetic multimerization of G3BP1, which is an essential scaffold protein for SG assembly.
evidence: This claim is supported by data from the manuscript and references to unpublished work (Yang, Mathieu et al., unpublished).

claim: Persistent or repetitive assembly of stress granules is cytotoxic.
source: In this system, which permits experimental control of SGs in living cells in the absence of exogenous stressors, we demonstrate that persistent or repetitive assembly of SGs is cytotoxic
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Chronic stress granule assembly is accompanied by the evolution of stress granules to cytoplasmic inclusions that recapitulate the pathology of ALS-FTD.
source: we demonstrate that persistent or repetitive assembly of SGs is cytotoxic and is accompanied by the evolution of SGs to cytoplasmic inclusions that recapitulate the pathology of ALS-FTD.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Genetic, pathologic, biophysical, and cell biological evidence has implicated disturbances in stress granules as a primary driver of several common neurodegenerative diseases, including ALS, FTD, and inclusion body myopathy (IBM).
source: Genetic, pathologic, biophysical, and cell biological evidence has implicated disturbances in stress granules as a primary driver of several common neurodegenerative diseases, including ALS, FTD, and inclusion body myopathy (IBM) (Molliex et al., 2015; Mackenzie et al., 2017; Taylor et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2016; Ramaswami et al., 2013; Buchan et al., 2013; Patel et al., 2015; Hackman et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: ALS, FTD, and IBM show substantial clinical and genetic overlap.
source: These diseases show substantial clinical and genetic overlap
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: ALS, FTD, and IBM share the hallmark histopathological feature of cytoplasmic inclusions composed of RNA-binding proteins and other constituents of ribonucleoprotein (RNP) granules in affected neurons and muscle cells.
source: These diseases show substantial clinical and genetic overlap and share the hallmark histopathological feature of cytoplasmic inclusions composed of RNA-binding proteins and other constituents of ribonucleoprotein (RNP) granules in affected neurons and muscle cells.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: A prominent feature of end-stage cytoplasmic pathology in ALS-FTD is ubiquitinated and phosphorylated forms of TDP-43.
source: A prominent feature of this end-stage cytoplasmic pathology is ubiquitinated and phosphorylated forms of TDP-43
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Other proteins co-localize with pathological inclusions in ALS-FTD, including related RNA-binding proteins and ubiquitin-binding proteins such as SQSTM1, UBQLN2, OPTN, and VCP.
source: although a host of other proteins co-localize with these pathological inclusions, including related RNA-binding proteins and ubiquitin-binding proteins such as SQSTM1, UBQLN2, OPTN, and VCP (Neumann et al., 2006; Mackenzie et al., 2007; Mackenzie and Neumann, 2016; Williams et al., 2012; Deng et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Many mutations that cause ALS-FTD and/or IBM impact RNA-binding proteins that are building blocks of stress granules (e.g., TDP-43, hnRNPA1, hnRNPA2B1, hnRNPDL, TIA1, matrin 3, and FUS).
source: Many mutations that cause ALS-FTD and/or IBM impact RNA-binding proteins that are building blocks of stress granules (e.g., TDP-43, hnRNPA1, hnRNPA2B1, hnRNPDL, TIA1, matrin 3, and FUS).
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: ALS-FTD mutations largely cluster in low-complexity, intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs).
source: Furthermore, these mutations largely cluster in low-complexity, intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs)
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: ALS-FTD mutations in RNA-binding proteins have been shown to change the dynamic properties of stress granules.
source: and in many cases have been shown to change the dynamic properties of stress granules (Mackenzie et al., 2017; Hackman et al., 2013; Kim et al., 2013; Liu-Yesucevitz et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Disease-causing mutations impact ubiquitin-binding proteins (e.g., UBQLN2, VCP, p62/SQSTM1, and OPTN) whose functions intersect with disassembly and/or clearance of stress granules.
source: Another set of disease-causing mutations impact ubiquitin-binding proteins (e.g., UBQLN2, VCP, p62/SQSTM1, and OPTN) whose functions intersect with disassembly and/or clearance of stress granules (Buchan et al., 2013; Dao et al., 2018; Chitiprolu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Pathological poly-dipeptides arising from repeat-expanded C9orf72 insinuate into stress granules and other membrane-less organelles, perturbing their dynamics and/or functions.
source: Furthermore, pathological poly-dipeptides arising from repeat-expanded C9orf72, the most common genetic cause of ALS-FTD, insinuate into stress granules and other membrane-less organelles, perturbing their dynamics and/or functions (Lee et al., 2016; Boeynaems et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: C9orf72 is the most common genetic cause of ALS-FTD.
source: Furthermore, pathological poly-dipeptides arising from repeat-expanded C9orf72, the most common genetic cause of ALS-FTD
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Several ALS-, FTD-, and IBM-causing mutations cause aberrant phase separation and change the biophysical and material properties of stress granules.
source: Several ALS-, FTD-, and IBM-causing mutations cause aberrant phase separation and change the biophysical and material properties of stress granules
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: ALS-FTD mutations generally result in poorly dynamic membrane-less organelles.
source: generally resulting in poorly dynamic membrane-less organelles
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: It has been suggested that poorly dynamic stress granules may evolve into the cytoplasmic pathology found in end-stage disease.
source: generally resulting in poorly dynamic membrane-less organelles that, it has been suggested, may evolve into the cytoplasmic pathology found in end-stage disease (Mackenzie et al., 2017; Buchan et al., 2013; Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from prior literature, indicated by 'it has been suggested'.

claim: No direct evidence has demonstrated that perturbation of phase separation is sufficient to drive neurotoxicity.
source: However, no direct evidence has demonstrated that perturbation of phase separation is sufficient to drive neurotoxicity
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this study.

claim: No direct evidence has demonstrated that ALS-FTD-associated inclusions represent the endpoint of a formerly dynamic stress granule.
source: or that ALS-FTD-associated inclusions represent the endpoint of a formerly dynamic stress granule.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this study.

claim: Models employing exogenous stressors (e.g., heat shock, arsenite) to initiate stress granule assembly have numerous nonspecific and pleiotropic effects.
source: Moreover, capitalizing on mechanistic links between stress granules and disease to identify therapeutic targets has been limited by models employing exogenous stressors (e.g., heat shock, arsenite) to initiate stress granule assembly, with numerous nonspecific and pleiotropic effects.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about limitations of current methods.

claim: Stress granules are comparatively large (~50 nm to ~3 μm) biomolecular condensates.
source: Stress granules are comparatively large (~50 nm to ~3 μm) biomolecular condensates
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Stress granules rapidly form in the cytoplasm in response to a wide variety of stressors.
source: Stress granules are comparatively large (~50 nm to ~3 μm) biomolecular condensates that rapidly form in the cytoplasm in response to a wide variety of stressors (Protter and Parker, 2016; Panas et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Stress granules are believed to arise at least in part through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS).
source: Like other RNP granules, stress granules are believed to arise at least in part through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS)
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: LLPS is a biophysical phenomenon in which RNA-protein complexes separate from the surrounding aqueous cytoplasm to create a functional cellular compartment with liquid properties.
source: a biophysical phenomenon in which RNA-protein complexes separate from the surrounding aqueous cytoplasm to create a functional cellular compartment with liquid properties (Molliex et al., 2015; Protter and Parker, 2016).
evidence: This is a definitional statement based on established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Stress granule assembly involves the dismantling of polysomes and reorganization of mRNPs into discrete cytoplasmic foci.
source: Stress granule assembly is a complex process that involves a cascade of events, including the dismantling of polysomes and reorganization of mRNPs into discrete cytoplasmic foci
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Stress granules contain >400 different protein constituents.
source: that contain >400 different protein constituents (Jain et al., 2016; Markmiller et al., 2018; Youn et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Stress granules contain >1800 different RNAs.
source: and >1800 different RNAs (Khong et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The assembly of RNP granules is driven in part by the collective behavior of many macromolecular interactions, including RNA-RNA interactions, protein-RNA interactions, conventional interactions between folded protein domains, and weak, transient interactions mediated by low complexity IDRs of proteins.
source: The assembly of RNP granules, including stress granules, is driven in part by the collective behavior of many macromolecular interactions, including RNA-RNA interactions, protein-RNA interactions, conventional interactions between folded protein domains, as well as weak, transient interactions mediated by low complexity IDRs of proteins – particularly those present in RNA-binding proteins (Banani et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The precise mechanisms that orchestrate the assembly of distinct types of RNP granules are largely unknown.
source: While there is consensus about the major underlying forces that drive RNP granule assembly, the precise mechanisms that orchestrate the assembly of distinct types of RNP granules are largely unknown
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: RNP granules and other biomolecular condensates are established and maintained by a small number of essential constituents defined as scaffolds, whereas the remaining constituents are considered clients.
source: In this conceptual framework, RNP granules and other biomolecular condensates are established and maintained by a small number of essential constituents defined as scaffolds, whereas the remaining constituents are considered clients (Banani et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a conceptual framework from prior literature, supported by citations.

claim: At least six proteins have been suggested to be 'essential' elements of stress granules.
source: Although at least six proteins have been suggested to be 'essential' elements of stress granules (Markmiller et al., 2018; Youn et al., 2018; Kedersha et al., 2016; Gilks et al., 2004; Kwon et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A whole-genome screen identified G3BP as a uniquely essential scaffold in stress granule assembly.
source: In related work that informs the study presented here, we performed a whole-genome screen that identified G3BP as a uniquely essential scaffold in stress granule assembly (Yang, Mathieu et al., unpublished).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to unpublished work by the authors.

claim: An oligomerization domain within G3BP that is essential to stress granule assembly could be functionally replaced by heterologous oligomerization domains.
source: Moreover, we found that an oligomerization domain within G3BP that is essential to stress granule assembly could be functionally replaced by heterologous oligomerization domains, which suggested the possibility of engineering temporal and spatial control of stress granule assembly without the confounding influences of stress (Yang, Mathieu et al., unpublished).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to unpublished work by the authors.

claim: OptoDroplets uses optogenetic oligomerization of proteins as a means to control intracellular LLPS.
source: We built upon a previously described system, termed 'OptoDroplets,' which uses optogenetic oligomerization of proteins as a means to control intracellular LLPS (Shin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a description of a prior system from the literature, supported by citations.

claim: In the OptoDroplets system, light-sensitive chimeric proteins are assembled from the IDRs of various RNP granule proteins combined with the light-sensitive oligomerization domain of Arabidopsis thaliana cryptochrome 2 (CRY2) photolyase homology region (PHR).
source: In this system, light-sensitive chimeric proteins are assembled from the IDRs of various RNP granule proteins combined with the light-sensitive oligomerization domain of Arabidopsis thaliana cryptochrome 2 (CRY2) photolyase homology region (PHR) to generate fusion proteins that undergo LLPS in living cells upon blue light activation.
evidence: This is a description of a prior system from the literature.

claim: Enforced aggregation of IDRs drives LLPS and leads to OptoDroplet formation.
source: Whereas enforced aggregation of IDRs drives LLPS and thereby leads to OptoDroplet formation
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about the OptoDroplet system.

claim: Droplets formed by the IDRs of any given RNP granule protein are not anticipated to initiate the full cascade of bona fide RNP granule assembly.
source: it is not anticipated that droplets formed by the IDRs of any given RNP granule protein will initiate the full cascade of bona fide RNP granule assembly.
evidence: This is a hypothesis or expectation based on understanding of the OptoDroplet system.

claim: Enforced LLPS of a scaffold protein would initiate a process that faithfully reconstitutes the assembly of a stress granule, whereas LLPS of a client protein would not.
source: However, we reasoned that adapting this OptoDroplet system might provide a means of testing the hypothesis that enforced LLPS of key stress granule constituents could distinguish between stress granule scaffolds and clients, in which LLPS of a scaffold protein would initiate a process that faithfully reconstitutes the assembly of a stress granule, whereas LLPS of a client protein would not.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that the authors tested in this study.

claim: Light-based activation of Opto-G3BP1 initiated the rapid assembly of dynamic, cytoplasmic, liquid granules.
source: Herein we report that light-based activation of Opto-G3BP1, a chimeric protein assembled from the IDR and RNA-binding domain of G3BP1 combined with CRY2PHR, initiated the rapid assembly of dynamic, cytoplasmic, liquid granules
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Opto-G3BP1-induced granules were composed of canonical stress granule components, including PABP, TDP-43, TIA1, TIAR, eIF4G, eIF3η, ataxin 2, GLE1, FUS, and polyadenylated RNA.
source: that were composed of canonical stress granule components, including PABP, TDP-43, TIA1, TIAR, eIF4G, eIF3η, ataxin 2, GLE1, FUS, and polyadenylated RNA
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1 and supplementary figures.

claim: Within seconds of blue light activation, Opto-G3BP1 in U2OS cells assembled into numerous, spherical cytoplasmic granules that exhibited liquid behaviors.
source: Within seconds of blue light activation, Opto-G3BP1 in U2OS cells assembled into numerous, spherical cytoplasmic granules that exhibited liquid behaviors (Figure 1b and Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1b and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: A 5-millisecond pulse of blue light using a 488 nm vector laser (~2.5 MW/cm2) was sufficient to initiate robust induction of cytoplasmic granules.
source: A 5-millisecond pulse of blue light using a 488 nm vector laser (~2.5 MW/cm2) was sufficient to initiate robust induction of these cytoplasmic granules
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Opto-G3BP1-induced granules spontaneously disassembled over a period of approximately 5 min.
source: and these granules spontaneously disassembled over a period of approximately 5 min (Figure 1b,c).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1b,c.

claim: Opto-G3BP1-induced granules exhibited liquid behaviors such as fusion to form larger granules and relaxation to a spherical shape.
source: These granules were highly dynamic, exhibiting liquid behaviors such as fusion to form larger granules and relaxation to a spherical shape (Video 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Video 2.

claim: Under the same conditions, Opto-Control expression remained diffuse, with a modest amount of nuclear and cytoplasmic clusters.
source: In contrast, under the same conditions, Opto-Control expression remained diffuse, with a modest amount of nuclear and cytoplasmic clusters (Figure 1b and Video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1b and Video 1.

claim: Recovery rates and mobile fractions of Opto-G3BP1 granules were very similar to the conventional stress granule marker G3BP1-GFP.
source: To confirm the dynamic nature of the optically induced granules, we performed fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) to monitor recovery rates and mobile fractions of individual granules (Figure 1d–f), finding that these properties were very similar between Opto-G3BP1 and the conventional stress granule marker G3BP1-GFP.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1d-f.

claim: Opto-G3BP1 localized to spontaneous stress granules induced by expression of ALS mutant proteins (FUS R521C, TDP-43 ΔNLS, TIA1 A381T) even in the absence of blue light activation.
source: Furthermore, Opto-G3BP1 localized to spontaneous stress granules induced by expression of ALS mutant proteins (FUS R521C, TDP-43 ΔNLS, TIA1 A381T) even in the absence of blue light activation, demonstrating that the Opto-G3BP1 protein behaves similarly to endogenous G3BP1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The stress granule marker GFP-TIA1 was dynamically recruited into optically induced granules following light-induced assembly.
source: Employing live cell imaging, we documented the dynamic recruitment of the stress granule marker GFP-TIA1 into optically induced granules following light-induced assembly (Figure 1g and Video 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1g and Video 3.

claim: Clusters of Opto-Control (olig) did not recruit GFP-TIA1.
source: In contrast, clusters of Opto-Control (olig), a modified form of the Opto-Control construct designed to produce abundant aggregates, did not recruit GFP-TIA1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Opto-Control (olig) clusters did not show dynamic behavior by FRAP.
source: nor did they show dynamic behavior by FRAP (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d–f).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1d-f.

claim: In cells expressing Opto-G3BP1, but not Opto-Control, all stress granule components examined (PABP, TDP-43, TIA1, TIAR, eIF4G, eIF3η, ataxin 2, GLE1, and FUS) were recruited to optically induced granules.
source: In cells expressing Opto-G3BP1, but not Opto-Control, all stress granule components that we examined, including PABP, TDP-43, TIA1, TIAR, eIF4G, eIF3η, ataxin 2, GLE1, and FUS, were recruited to optically induced granules (Figure 1h–i and Figure 1—figure supplement 2a–g).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1h-i and Figure 1—figure supplement 2a-g.

claim: Polyadenylated mRNAs were recruited into optically induced granules that assembled after blue light stimulation.
source: We found that polyadenylated mRNAs were recruited into optically induced granules that assembled after blue light stimulation but showed no relocalization in cells expressing Opto-Control (Figure 1j).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1j.

claim: Optically induced Opto-G3BP1 granules are stress granules composed of mRNAs and RNA-binding proteins, including ALS-associated proteins such as TDP-43, ataxin 2, GLE1, FUS, and TIA1.
source: These findings indicate that optically induced Opto-G3BP1 granules are stress granules composed of mRNAs and RNA-binding proteins, including ALS-associated proteins such as TDP-43, ataxin 2, GLE1, FUS, and TIA1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 1 and supplementary figures.

claim: Knockout of endogenous G3BP1 and G3BP2 in U2OS cells abolished stress granule assembly in response to arsenite.
source: Consistent with prior reports, knockout of endogenous G3BP1 and G3BP2 in U2OS cells abolished stress granule assembly in response to arsenite (Kedersha et al., 2016) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3a and consistent with prior literature.

claim: Opto-G3BP1 (or Opto-G3BP2) substantially restored stress granule assembly in response to blue light in G3BP1/G3BP2 double knockout cells.
source: When introduced into these G3BP1/G3BP2 double knockout cells, Opto-G3BP1 (or the analogous chimeric protein Opto-G3BP2) substantially restored stress granule assembly in response to blue light activation, demonstrating that the scaffolding activity of G3BP1 in the chimeric protein is functionally intact (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b,c).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3b,c.

claim: Opto-FUS and Opto-TDP-43 assembled into droplets with blue light activation.
source: Opto-FUS [CRY2PHR-mCherry-FUS(IDR)] and Opto-TDP-43 [CRY2PHR-mCherry-TDP-43(IDR)] did assemble into droplets with blue light activation, as previously reported (Shin et al., 2017)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and consistent with prior literature.

claim: OptoDroplets formed by Opto-FUS and Opto-TDP-43 did not recruit stress granule constituents G3BP1 and PABP.
source: but these OptoDroplets did not recruit stress granule constituents commonly used as markers, including G3BP1 and PABP (Figure 1—figure supplement 4a–c)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4a-c.

claim: OptoDroplets formed by Opto-FUS and Opto-TDP-43 were negative for stress granule constituents VCP, SQSTM1, and OPTN.
source: and were also negative for stress granule constituents VCP, SQSTM1, and the related protein OPTN (Figure 1—figure supplement 4d,e).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4d,e.

claim: Constructs containing the IDR and RNA recognition motifs of FUS or TDP-43 assembled into droplets upon blue light activation, but these droplets were negative for stress granule markers.
source: Similarly, constructs containing the IDR and RNA recognition motifs of FUS or TDP-43 [CRY2PHR-mCherry-FUS (1–371 aa); CRY2PHR-mCherry-TDP-43 (106–414 aa)] assembled into droplets upon blue light activation, but these droplets were also negative for stress granule markers (Figure 1—figure supplement 4f,g).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4f,g.

claim: Expression of Opto-constructs using full-length FUS or TDP-43 did not produce stress granules with blue light activation.
source: Expression of Opto-constructs using full-length FUS or TDP-43 [CRY2PHR-mCherry-FUS(FL); CRY2PHR-mCherry-TDP-43(FL)] did not produce stress granules with blue light activation (Figure 1—figure supplement 4f,g).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4f,g.

claim: Opto-TIA1 assembled into droplets with blue light activation, but did not drive the assembly of stress granules.
source: Finally, Opto-TIA1, which represents fusion of CRY2 with TIA1 (CRY2PHR-mCherry-TIA1), also assembled into droplets with blue light activation, but did not drive the assembly of stress granules, as illustrated by lack of colocalization with stress granule markers (Figure 1—figure supplement 4h–j).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4h-j.

claim: RNP granule assembly cannot be driven by enforced LLPS of any random constituent, but depends upon specific constituents.
source: These data indicate that RNP granule assembly cannot be driven by enforced LLPS of any random constituent, but depends upon specific constituents.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: LLPS initiated by scaffold proteins (e.g., G3BP1) has the capacity to initiate a membrane-less organelle, whereas client proteins (e.g., FUS, TDP-43, TIA1), even when forced to undergo LLPS, cannot reconstitute such a complex assembly.
source: This conclusion is consistent with the proposition that LLPS initiated by scaffold proteins (e.g., G3BP1) has the capacity to initiate a membrane-less organelle, whereas client proteins (e.g., FUS, TDP-43, TIA1), even when forced to undergo LLPS, cannot reconstitute such a complex assembly (Banani et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data, consistent with a conceptual framework from prior literature.

claim: There is a strong positive correlation between blue light intensity and induction of OptoGranules.
source: As predicted, we observed a strong positive correlation between blue light intensity and induction of OptoGranules (Figure 2a,b)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 2a,b.

claim: There is a strong positive correlation between Opto-G3BP1 expression level and induction of OptoGranules.
source: and, independently, a strong positive correlation between Opto-G3BP1 expression level and induction of OptoGranules (Figure 2c,d).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 2c,d.

claim: The OptoGranule system is highly tunable.
source: Thus, the OptoGranule system is highly tunable, a useful feature for a variety of studies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 2a-d.

claim: Treatment with cycloheximide strongly mitigated the formation of arsenite-induced stress granules and the formation of light-induced OptoGranules.
source: We determined that treatment with cycloheximide, which traps translating mRNAs within polysomes, strongly mitigated the formation of arsenite-induced stress granules and the formation of light-induced OptoGranules (Figure 2e,f)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 2e,f.

claim: OptoGranule formation is dependent on polysome disassembly.
source: indicating that OptoGranule formation is dependent on polysome disassembly and further illustrating commonality with conventional stress granules.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cycloheximide experiment data in Figure 2e,f.

claim: Formation of arsenite-induced stress granules was blocked by ISRIB.
source: We found that formation of arsenite-induced stress granules was blocked by ISRIB, as previously documented (Sidrauski et al., 2015)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 2e,f and consistent with prior literature.

claim: The formation of light-induced OptoGranules was unaffected by ISRIB treatment.
source: whereas the formation of light-induced OptoGranules was unaffected by ISRIB treatment (Figure 2e,f).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 2e,f.

claim: Western blotting showed minimal phosphorylated eIF2α accompanying OptoGranule assembly.
source: Consistent with this finding, Western blotting also showed minimal phosphorylated eIF2α accompanying OptoGranule assembly (Figure 2g, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 2g and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: OptoGranule formation depends upon the recruitment of mRNPs from polysomes, but this assembly occurs downstream and independent of the evolutionarily conserved integrated stress response regulated by eIF2α.
source: Thus, OptoGranule formation depends upon the recruitment of mRNPs from polysomes, but this assembly occurs downstream and independent of the evolutionarily conserved integrated stress response regulated by eIF2α.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 2e-g.

claim: OptoGranule formation is not driven by the classic signaling pathway for stress granule formation, which increases the concentration of free, uncoated RNA in the cytoplasm, but rather by oligomerization of G3BP1, which increases the valency for RNA binding.
source: This observation is consistent with the notion that OptoGranule formation is not driven by the classic signaling pathway for stress granule formation, which increases the concentration of free, uncoated RNA in the cytoplasm, but rather by oligomerization of G3BP1, which increases the valency for RNA binding.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data, representing an inference about the mechanism.

claim: Continuous induction of OptoGranules using a blue-light LED array resulted in progressive loss of cell viability reflected by progressive loss of crystal violet staining and depletion of ATP levels.
source: We found that continuous induction of OptoGranules using a blue-light LED array resulted in progressive loss of cell viability reflected by progressive loss of crystal violet staining and depletion of ATP levels (Figure 3a,b).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 3a,b.

claim: Chronic exposure to blue light resulted in a moderate amount of cytotoxicity in cells expressing Opto-Control or parental U2OS cells.
source: However, we also noted that chronic exposure to blue light resulted in a moderate amount of cytotoxicity in cells expressing Opto-Control or parental U2OS cells (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 3b.

claim: Cells expressing Opto-G3BP1 exhibited significantly greater loss of viability upon exposure to blue light than cells expressing Opto-Control or parental U2OS cells.
source: Although cells expressing Opto-G3BP1 exhibited significantly greater loss of viability upon exposure to blue light than cells expressing Opto-Control or parental U2OS cells
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 3b.

claim: Persistent OptoGranule assembly (2 s on, 12 s off) resulted in significant loss of viability in cells expressing Opto-G3BP1, with comparatively greatly reduced toxicity in cells expressing Opto-Control.
source: Interestingly, persistent OptoGranule assembly under these conditions (2 s on, 12 s off) resulted in significant loss of viability in cells expressing Opto-G3BP1, with comparatively greatly reduced toxicity in cells expressing Opto-Control (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 3c.

claim: Chronic, intermittent OptoGranule assembly (10 s blue light pulse followed by 10 min of rest) greatly mitigated background toxicity due to blue light exposure and revealed significant toxicity in cells expressing Opto-G3BP1 compared to cells expressing Opto-Control.
source: This paradigm of chronic, intermittent OptoGranule assembly, which may more closely reflect physiological, chronic, intermittent stress, greatly mitigated background toxicity due to blue light exposure and revealed significant toxicity in cells expressing Opto-G3BP1 compared to cells expressing Opto-Control (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 3d.

claim: Chronic persistent or chronic intermittent stress granule assembly is intrinsically cytotoxic, independent of exogenous stressors.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that chronic persistent or chronic intermittent stress granule assembly is intrinsically cytotoxic, independent of exogenous stressors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 3a-d.

claim: Disease pathology in tissue from patients with ALS and FTD is marked by deposits of ubiquitin, ubiquitin-binding proteins, and TDP-43 that is cleaved and abnormally phosphorylated at Ser409/410.
source: Disease pathology in tissue from patients with ALS and FTD is marked by deposits of ubiquitin, ubiquitin-binding proteins, and TDP-43 that is cleaved and abnormally phosphorylated at Ser409/410 (Neumann et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Newly formed OptoGranules were initially immunopositive for TDP-43 and ubiquitin, but immunonegative for phospho-TDP-43 and ubiquitin-binding proteins.
source: Although OptoGranules were initially immunopositive for TDP-43 (as are conventional arsenite-induced stress granules) and ubiquitin, they were immunonegative for phospho-TDP-43 and ubiquitin-binding proteins (Figure 3e–i).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 3e-i.

claim: OptoGranules were immunopositive for staining by anti-A11, a conformation-specific antibody that recognizes amyloid oligomer.
source: OptoGranules were, however, immunopositive for staining by anti-A11, a conformation-specific antibody that recognizes amyloid oligomer, a feature also shared by conventional stress granules (Figure 3e–i and Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 3e-i and Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: OptoGranules showed time-dependent reduction in dynamics as assessed by FRAP.
source: Remarkably, the characteristics of OptoGranules changed during chronic assembly. First, OptoGranules showed time-dependent reduction in dynamics as assessed by FRAP (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d.

claim: After approximately two hours of OptoGranule assembly, these granules showed immunopositivity using two distinct anti-phospho-TDP-43 antibodies.
source: Moreover, we observed that immunopositivity for TDP-43, A11, and ubiquitin gradually increased over time, and after approximately two hours of OptoGranule assembly, these granules showed immunopositivity using two distinct anti-phospho-TDP-43 antibodies (Figure 3f–i, Figure 3—figure supplement 1e,f).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 3f-i and Figure 3—figure supplement 1e,f.

claim: After approximately five hours of chronic OptoGranule assembly, there was a significant increase in immunopositivity using antibodies to phospho-TDP-43 and the ubiquitin-binding proteins SQSTM1 and VCP.
source: Moreover, after approximately five hours of chronic OptoGranule assembly, we observed a significant increase in immunopositivity using antibodies to phospho-TDP-43 and the ubiquitin-binding proteins SQSTM1 and VCP, illustrating further evolution of these structures (Figure 3g–i).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 3g-i.

claim: Cell death associated with chronic OptoGranule assembly is preceded by the evolution of OptoGranules into cytoplasmic inclusions that recapitulate features that are pathognomonic for ALS-FTD.
source: Thus, not only does chronic OptoGranule assembly cause a loss of cell viability, but cell death is preceded by the evolution of OptoGranules into cytoplasmic inclusions that recapitulate features that are pathognomonic for ALS-FTD.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 3.

claim: iPSC-derived neurons assembled conventional stress granules that were positive for TIA1 and TDP-43 in response to arsenite or heat shock stresses.
source: In response to arsenite or heat shock stresses, these iPSC-derived neurons assembled conventional stress granules that were positive for TIA1 and TDP-43, indicating that they were suitable for examining the consequences of chronic stress granules (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1c.

claim: In mRuby-Opto-G3BP1-expressing neurons, blue light activation induced the assembly of OptoGranules indistinguishable from those observed in U2OS cells.
source: In mRuby-Opto-G3BP1-expressing neurons, blue light activation induced the assembly of OptoGranules indistinguishable from those observed in U2OS cells (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1d and Videos 4 and 5).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1d, and Videos 4 and 5.

claim: Chronic induction of OptoGranules in neurons resulted in progressive loss of neuronal viability.
source: Chronic induction of OptoGranules following transient introduction of mRuby-Opto-G3BP1 resulted in progressive loss of neuronal viability (Figure 4c)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 4c.

claim: Chronic induction of OptoGranules in neurons resulted in the formation of neuronal cytoplasmic inclusions that were immunopositive for TDP-43, A11, and ubiquitin, with time-dependent immunopositivity for phosphorylated TDP-43 and SQSTM1.
source: and the formation of neuronal cytoplasmic inclusions that were immunopositive for TDP-43, A11, and ubiquitin, with time-dependent immunopositivity for phosphorylated TDP-43 and SQSTM1 (Figure 4d–i, Figure 4—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 4d-i and Figure 4—figure supplement 1e.

claim: Chronic OptoGranule induction recapitulates the evolution of ALS-FTD pathology and neurotoxicity in human iPSC-derived neurons.
source: Thus, chronic OptoGranule induction recapitulates the evolution of ALS-FTD pathology and neurotoxicity in human iPSC-derived neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 4 and supplementary figures.

claim: OptoGranules and OptoDroplets are fundamentally different.
source: Beyond this similarity, however, OptoDroplets and OptoGranules are fundamentally different.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data and discussion.

claim: G3BP is a uniquely essential central scaffold protein for stress granules, in contrast to TIA1, TDP-43, FUS and many others, which are client proteins.
source: In unpublished work that strongly informed the development of OptoGranules, we identified G3BP as a uniquely essential central scaffold protein for stress granules, in contrast to TIA1, TDP-43, FUS and many others, which are client proteins (Yang, Mathieu et al., unpublished).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to unpublished work by the authors.

claim: Client proteins often reside in multiple biomolecular condensates with distinct identities.
source: The differences in the assemblies formed by client proteins versus those formed by scaffold proteins make sense, since client proteins often reside in multiple biomolecular condensates with distinct identities.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Enforced LLPS of a scaffold protein initiates the cascade of events that seeds the assembly of a full-fledged, complex stress granule.
source: In contrast, enforced LLPS of a scaffold protein initiates the cascade of events that seeds the assembly of a full-fledged, complex stress granule.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data and discussion.

claim: OptoDroplets formed by Opto-TDP-43, Opto-FUS, and Opto-TIA1 have their biophysical origin in CRY2 oligomerization that forces the IDRs of these proteins to self-associate and initiate a phase transition.
source: OptoDroplets formed by Opto-TDP-43, Opto-FUS, and Opto-TIA1 have their biophysical origin in CRY2 oligomerization that presumably forces the IDRs of these proteins to self-associate and initiate a phase transition (Shin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement based on understanding of the OptoDroplet system, supported by citations.

claim: Activation of Opto-G3BP1 forms granules because CRY2-based multimerization increases the valency of G3BP, permitting it to engage with another scaffolding element (i.e., a class of RNAs), and these interactions create a seed that subsequently undergoes a phase transition that mediates subsequent further assembly of a stress granule.
source: In contrast, activation of Opto-G3BP1 forms granules because CRY2-based multimerization (specifically via the replaced NTF2L domain) increases the valency of G3BP, permitting it to engage with another scaffolding element (i.e., a class of RNAs), and these interactions create a seed that subsequently undergoes a phase transition that mediates subsequent further assembly of a stress granule.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation based on the data and understanding of the system.

claim: LLPS-mediated assembly, dynamics, and material properties of stress granules must be viewed within the context of a larger cellular network of membrane-less organelles.
source: However, we must emphatically note that LLPS-mediated assembly, dynamics, and material properties of stress granules must be viewed within the context of a larger cellular network of membrane-less organelles, which include a wide variety of nuclear and cytoplasmic RNP granules.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Membrane-less organelles are now recognized as functionally relevant biomolecular condensates that underlie different segregated biochemistries within a single cell.
source: Indeed, membrane-less organelles are now recognized as functionally relevant biomolecular condensates that underlie different segregated biochemistries within a single cell (Banani et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The material properties (e.g., assembly/disassembly rates, mobility, viscosity) of membrane-less organelles likely influence their functions.
source: Furthermore, their material properties (e.g., assembly/disassembly rates, mobility, viscosity) likely influence these functions
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: The data supports the hypothesis that ALS-FTD arises from disturbances in the dynamics and material properties of membrane-less organelles.
source: indeed, the data presented here supports the burgeoning hypothesis that ALS-FTD arises from disturbances in the dynamics and material properties of membrane-less organelles, with devastating consequences over time.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: Disease may reflect simultaneous pathological disturbance of multiple membrane-less organelles that arises by derangement of a network of multiple, independent phases.
source: Extending this hypothesis, we speculate that disease may reflect simultaneous pathological disturbance of multiple membrane-less organelles that arises by derangement of a network of multiple, independent phases.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: Interconnections between membrane-less organelles likely reflect communication across different types of membrane-less compartments based on rapid, dynamic exchange of macromolecules (e.g., RNA and RNA-binding proteins) and small molecules that act as vehicles to communicate material states throughout the network.
source: These interconnections likely reflect communication across different types of membrane-less compartments based on rapid, dynamic exchange of macromolecules (e.g., RNA and RNA-binding proteins) and small molecules that act as vehicles to communicate material states throughout the network.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: Perturbation of one phase-separated compartment (stress granules) alters the properties and function of a distinct phase-separated structure (the nuclear pore).
source: An example of this is seen in the recent report that perturbation of one phase-separated compartment (stress granules) alters the properties and function of a distinct phase-separated structure (the nuclear pore) (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Primary disturbances in the material properties of one node of the network (e.g., stress granules) may lead to secondary disturbances that are propagated throughout the entire network of membrane-less organelles.
source: With such a system-wide regulation, primary disturbances in the material properties of one node of the network (e.g., stress granules) may lead to secondary disturbances that are propagated throughout the entire network of membrane-less organelles.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: Opto-G3BP1 is a chimeric protein assembled from the IDR and RNA-binding domain of G3BP1 combined with CRY2PHR.
source: Herein we report that light-based activation of Opto-G3BP1, a chimeric protein assembled from the IDR and RNA-binding domain of G3BP1 combined with CRY2PHR
evidence: This is a description of the Opto-G3BP1 construct developed in this study.

claim: G3BP1 has an N-terminal 142-amino acid dimerization domain, termed the NTF2L domain, that is essential for nucleation of stress granule assembly.
source: G3BP1 has an N-terminal 142-amino acid dimerization domain, termed the NTF2L domain, that is essential for nucleation of stress granule assembly.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field and unpublished work by the authors.

claim: The NTF2L domain of G3BP1 can be replaced by generic dimerization domains, and the resulting chimeric proteins are able to fully nucleate stress granule assembly in living cells.
source: Remarkably, the NTF2L domain can be replaced by generic dimerization domains, and the resulting chimeric proteins are able to fully nucleate stress granule assembly in living cells (Yang, Mathieu et al., unpublished).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to unpublished work by the authors.

claim: Opto-G3BP1 and endogenous G3BP1 have comparable expression levels in stable U2OS cell lines.
source: We next generated U2OS cell lines stably expressing Opto-Control or Opto-G3BP1 constructs with comparable expression levels of Opto-G3BP1 and endogenous G3BP1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Conventional stress granule formation is typically linked to the disassembly of translating polysomes.
source: Given that conventional stress granule formation is typically linked to the disassembly of translating polysomes (Panas et al., 2016)
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Cycloheximide traps translating mRNAs within polysomes.
source: We determined that treatment with cycloheximide, which traps translating mRNAs within polysomes
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about the mechanism of cycloheximide.

claim: eIF2α phosphorylation integrates stress granule formation downstream of a variety of stressors, such as arsenite and heat shock.
source: We next tested the role of eIF2α phosphorylation, which integrates stress granule formation downstream of a variety of stressors, such as arsenite and heat shock (Panas et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: ISRIB binds eIF2B and interrupts eIF2α-mediated translational control.
source: We used the small molecule ISRIB, which binds eIF2B and interrupts eIF2α-mediated translational control (Sidrauski et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about the mechanism of ISRIB, supported by citations.

claim: OptoGranule formation is not driven by the classic signaling pathway for stress granule formation regulated by eIF2α.
source: Thus, OptoGranule formation depends upon the recruitment of mRNPs from polysomes, but this assembly occurs downstream and independent of the evolutionarily conserved integrated stress response regulated by eIF2α.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing that ISRIB does not block OptoGranule formation.

claim: The presence of A11 immunopositivity in newly formed stress granules suggests that non-pathological amyloid oligomers are present in the mRNPs recruited to these structures.
source: The presence of A11 immunopositivity in newly formed stress granules suggests that non-pathological amyloid oligomers are present in the mRNPs recruited to these structures, perhaps arising from the prion-like low complexity domains of RNA-binding proteins coating these mRNPs.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the A11 immunopositivity data.

claim: Close packing of physiological amyloids in the condensed liquid state of persistent stress granules risks seeding the assembly of pathological amyloids, particularly for proteins like TDP-43 that can adopt highly stable structures.
source: While these are presumably physiological amyloids, it is conceivable that their close packing in the condensed liquid state of persistent stress granules risks seeding the assembly of pathological amyloids, particularly for proteins like TDP-43 that can adopt highly stable structures.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: The anti-phospho-TDP-43 antibodies specifically recognize phosphorylation of TDP-43 at residues Ser409/410.
source: The anti-phospho-TDP-43 antibodies specifically recognize phosphorylation of TDP-43 at residues Ser409/410
evidence: This is a statement about the specificity of the antibodies used in the study.

claim: Phosphorylation of TDP-43 at Ser409/410 is a pathological signature specific to a spectrum of sporadic and familial forms of TDP-43 proteinopathies, including ALS-FTD.
source: a pathological signature specific to a spectrum of sporadic and familial forms of TDP-43 proteinopathies, including ALS-FTD (Neumann et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: iPSC-derived neurons generated in this study had a cortical molecular identity.
source: We next examined the consequence of protracted stress granule assembly in a more disease-relevant, neuronal context by generating human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neurons, which we verified had a cortical molecular identity (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a,b.

claim: With continuous stimulation, OptoGranules in iPSC neurons evolved into neuronal cytoplasmic inclusions that were positive for phospho-TDP-43, A11, ubiquitin, and SQSTM1.
source: With continuous stimulation, these OptoGranules further evolved into neuronal cytoplasmic inclusions that were positive for phospho-TDP-43, A11, ubiquitin, and SQSTM1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2c–f).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2c-f.
